agriculture.def: The raising of crops and animals on purpose for food, fiber and other products.

intensive-agriculture.def: Farming that puts many inputs (labor, money, machines, fertilizer, water) into each unit of land to get a large output from it, as in market gardening near Rotterdam.

extensive-agriculture.def: Farming that uses few inputs on each unit of land, spread over large areas, as in ranching on the Pampas of Argentina.

market-gardening.def: Intensive growing of fruits, vegetables and flowers for nearby city markets; also called truck farming.

plantation-agriculture.def: Intensive farming of one crop, such as oil palm, bananas or tea, on a large estate, usually in the tropics, for sale far away.

mixed-crop-livestock.def: Intensive farming that raises crops and animals on the same farm, often feeding the crops to the animals, as in the US Corn Belt.

shifting-cultivation.def: Extensive farming in which people clear and burn a forest plot, farm it for a few years and then move on while the old plot rests and regrows; also called slash and burn or swidden.

nomadic-herding.def: Extensive agriculture in which people move herds of animals to fresh grass and water with the seasons, as in Mongolia; also called pastoral nomadism.

ranching.def: Extensive raising of cattle or sheep that graze large areas of fixed land, usually for sale to distant buyers.

mediterranean-agriculture.def: Farming suited to hot, dry summers and mild, rainy winters, growing crops such as olives, grapes and citrus in places like southern Spain and central Chile.

irrigation.def: Supplying water to crops by canals, pipes, ditches or sprinklers, so land can be farmed where rain alone is not enough.
